reason: The general mechanism is credible and observed in the wild. Crafted assistant links use URL parameters to pre-fill prompts that poison an assistant's memory or recommendations. Microsoft's Security Blog (2026-02-10) documented 'Summarize with AI' links instructing assistants to remember or recommend a company, and MITRE ATLAS v2026.09 added AML.T0131 with case study AML.CS0072. However, the development-context path (deep links in READMEs or issues biasing an agent's memory or dependency choices) is extrapolated, with no coding-agent occurrence recorded. ATLAS lists no mitigation, and RMD-ASSISTLINK-001 is only 'signal' maturity. Watch until a coding-agent instance is reported.

evidence.summary: AML.T0131 Crafted AI Assistant Links and case study AML.CS0072; no mitigation listed (recorded in RMD-ASSISTLINK-001).
Real-world pre-filled prompt memory poisoning in consumer assistants, with Copilot mitigations.
signal; treat assistant deep links as untrusted input, no auto-open, confirm before executing a pre-filled prompt, provenance on memory writes.

model_assessment.assessment: An input-channel and memory-provenance mechanism. Provider-side mitigations exist for Copilot only.

remedy_assessment.assessment: Signal-level, low-risk control. Applies only where assistants have memory or accept pre-filled prompts.

reopen_triggers: coding-agent instance of crafted-link memory or recommendation poisoning
ATLAS adds a mitigation for AML.T0131
major harness ships pre-fill confirmation or memory provenance controls
